answer: An anchor-delay bond makes each identity run one chain per epoch, anchored to the epoch seed. The chain cannot be rushed or precomputed; finishing it yields a pearl, proof of sequential time. A pearl tied to another key is rejected and burns the bond, and wandering off schedule loses the bond. Each identity locks 40 and pays 30: first fake 70, thousandth 70, so 1,000 fakes cost 70,000 against a 40,000 pool. An honest agent pays 30 once.
